question: When is the first day of classes for Spring 2027?
reference_answer: Spring 2027 classes begin January 19, 2027.

evidence.quote: January 19 | Classes Begin

question: How do I find the last day to drop my classes?
reference_answer: Log in to myUCCS, go to Register for Classes (add/drop), find My Class Schedule, and select the Enrollment Deadlines link next to the course.

evidence.quote: You can locate your course's specific deadlines by logging into your myUCCS portal, go to 'Register for Classes (add/drop)', locate 'My Class Schedule', and select the 'Enrollment Deadlines' link next to each course.

question: Can I get a full refund if I drop a class before the census date?
reference_answer: Yes. Dropping by the census date qualifies for a full refund of tuition and most course fees.

evidence.quote: The Census Date is the last day to drop without penalty and receive a full refund of tuition and most course fees.

question: What happens if I drop a class after the census date?
reference_answer: It counts as a withdrawal: the course is non-refundable and gets a W notation on your transcript.

evidence.quote: Courses that are withdrawn from after their census date date are non-refundable and are assigned with an official notation of ‘W’ (withdrawn).

question: Can I drop a class through myUCCS?
reference_answer: Yes. You can drop courses in your myUCCS portal until 11:59 p.m. (MT) on each course's census date.

evidence.quote: Students can drop courses in their myUCCS portal from their initial enrollment appointment until 11:59pm (MT) on each course's census date.

question: since dropping a class is free until finals, should i wait until then?
reference_answer: No. Dropping is only free until the census date, which is the last day to drop without penalty and receive a full refund of tuition and most course fees.

evidence.quote: The Census Date is the last day to drop without penalty and receive a full refund of tuition and most course fees.

question: How does the waitlist work?
reference_answer: Students on the waitlist are automatically enrolled if a seat becomes available or enrollment limits are increased.

evidence.quote: Students on the waitlist are automatically enrolled in the class if a seat becomes available or enrollment limits are increased.

question: When do waitlists close?
reference_answer: After the published last day to waitlist, waitlists are no longer available, and instructor approval is required to enroll in a closed course.

evidence.quote: After this date has passed, waitlists are no longer available. Instructor approval is required to enroll in a course that is closed (at capacity) after this date.

question: since im on the waitlist, does that mean im guaranteed a spot in the class?
reference_answer: No. Being on the waitlist doesn't guarantee a seat. Waitlisted students are only enrolled automatically if a seat becomes available or enrollment limits are increased.

evidence.quote: Students on the waitlist are automatically enrolled in the class if a seat becomes available or enrollment limits are increased.

question: Can I enroll in a class after the census date?
reference_answer: Only with approval: after the census date, adding a course requires approval from the instructor, the academic dean, and the Bursar.

evidence.quote: The census date of a course or session is also the last day to enroll without approvals. Course adds after this date require instructor, academic dean, & Bursar approval.

question: How can I see my transfer credits?
reference_answer: Log in to myUCCS and go to Degree Audit to see how your credits transferred.

evidence.quote: Log in to your myUCCS account and go to Degree Audit to see how your credits transferred.

question: How long does it take for transfer credits to appear?
reference_answer: Allow three to five business days for transfer credit to be posted.

reference_answer: The first e-bills are uploaded January 14 for students who register before that date.

question: When is the Spring 2027 tuition payment deadline?
reference_answer: February 3, before 5 p.m. Students enrolled on or before that day must pay their balance in full or enroll in a deferred payment plan, or late fines may apply.

evidence.quote: February 3 | Due Date BEFORE 5pm, students who enroll on or before this day must pay their balance in-full or enroll in a deferred payment plan; otherwise, late fines may be applied.

question: When will I receive my financial aid refund?
reference_answer: Within three to five business days after disbursement, by direct deposit or check depending on the refund method you requested.

evidence.quote: Refunds from financial aid funds are issued within 3-5 business days from disbursement via direct deposit or check, depending on the refund method requested.

question: When will I know my residence hall assignment for Fall?

question: Are first-year students required to live on campus?
reference_answer: First-year, first-time students under 21 are required to live on campus with a meal plan.

evidence.quote: All first-year, first-time students under the age of 21 are required to live on campus with a meal plan.

question: Can I request a housing accommodation because of a disability?
reference_answer: Yes. Disability Services reviews housing accommodation requests on a student-by-student basis, based on the documentation of the disability.

evidence.quote: Disability Services reviews requests for Housing Accommodations on a student-by-student basis, depending on the medical information provided in the documentation of a disability.

question: Can a past-due balance prevent me from registering for classes?
reference_answer: Yes. A past-due balance greater than $500 puts a hold on your account that prevents adding courses.
